summary: Streaming chat responses disconnect or stall mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) for NovaAI on Dedicated capacity
description: Issue summary: Customer reports streaming chat responses disconnecting or stalling mid-generation when using SSE or WebSocket streaming endpoints. Impact: Customer's product shows incomplete assistant messages to end users causing UX breakage and user-facing errors. Environment: Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated pool) in prod - us-east. Observed start time: ~2026-03-01 09:15 UTC when NovaAI first reported widespread hangs. Steps to reproduce: 1) Open a streaming chat session against the Redwood streaming endpoint (SSE or WebSocket) pinned to customer's dedicated model. 2) Send multi-turn prompts that elicit >512-token responses. 3) Observe that streaming begins, tokens stream for a few hundred tokens, then connection either drops with a 5xx from gateway or stalls with no new tokens for >30s while connection remains open. Observed behavior: mid-generation stalls (no new data) or abrupt disconnects. Expected behavior: continuous token streaming until final token or graceful end-of-stream event. Logs & traces: customer provided sample request IDs; internal logs show repeated 'kvcache refill' and 'stream-heartbeat timeout' around same timeframe. Relevant customer request IDs: req-neo-20260301-1132, req-neo-20260301-1158. Additional context: This started after a recent autoscaling change to the dedicated pool and simultaneous rollout of streaming-proxy 2.14.2. Similar symptoms appeared in a small number of other dedicated customers but with lower frequency.
steps_to_reproduce: Use SSE or WebSocket streaming endpoint pinned to customer-dedicated pool
Send multi-turn prompts generating long outputs (>512 tokens)
Observe streaming stalls after ~200-800 tokens or abrupt disconnect with 502/503
Reproduce consistently with model redwood-instruct-13b-8k on dedicated pool (NovaAI)
impact: End users see truncated assistant messages or fail to receive completions; NovaAI reports significant degradation to live chat feature during peak traffic windows. Estimated affected sessions: ~8-12% of streaming sessions during the incident window for NovaAI's dedicated pool.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Streaming-proxy 2.14.2 heartbeat/backpressure change causes prolonged stalls under certain request-size patterns.
Hypothesis 2: Serving runtime kv-cache refill race with eviction leads to temporary stall while requests wait for cache fill; more likely for long-generation requests.
Correlation: Higher incidence on dedicated pools with contiguous high-load segments (NovaAI peak times).
Telemetry: Increase in 'stream-heartbeat timeout' and 'kvcache refill delay' metrics starting 2026-03-01 08:50 UTC coincident with autoscaler tweak and proxy rollout.
Canary rollback to 2.14.1 decreased error rate by ~60% for the canary nodes (metrics from 2026-03-01 10:00-12:00 UTC).

Reproduced locally: synthetic load test with long responses reproduces stall ~30% when running streaming-proxy 2.14.2 + autoscaler configured with aggressive downscale. Lowering downscale threshold reduced reproduction rate.

workaround: Temporary mitigation: roll streaming-proxy back to 2.14.1 for affected dedicated pools and adjust autoscaler downscale aggressiveness to reduce pod churn. For NovaAI we rolled back canary and are scheduling full rollback if hotfix not validated within 24h.
resolution_notes: In progress. Patch submitted to serving-runtime to fix kvcache refill race (PR #8426). Once PR merges, we will stage hotfix to dedicated pools with coordinated streaming-proxy rollback plan. Post-deploy verification: monitor stream-success-rate, stream-heartbeat-timeout, and kvcache-refill-delay for 24h. Follow-up: add unit/integration tests for kvcache concurrency and update runbook to include streaming-heartbeat thresholds. If hotfix validated, close ticket and notify NovaAI with root cause and remediation steps.
postmortem_action_items: Complete PR #8426 and merge after review
